title: CBSE Class 9 Mathematics Mock Paper 4 (NCERT Exemplar & Periodic Assessment HOTS)
description: Challenging, higher-order thinking paper drawn from NCERT Exemplar and authentic School Periodic Assessments (PA-1 & PA-2). Features multi-step algebraic synthesis, coordinate proofs, and real-world geometric modeling.

questions.prompt: Points P(-1, 1), Q(3, -4), R(1, -1), S(-2, -3) and T(-4, 4) are plotted on a Cartesian grid. Which of these points lie strictly in the fourth quadrant?
questions.answer: (b) Q and R
questions.markingScheme: • Quadrant IV points satisfy x > 0 and y < 0. For Q(3, -4), 3 > 0, -4 < 0. For R(1, -1), 1 > 0, -1 < 0. [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Points in Quadrant IV have positive abscissa and negative ordinate (+, -).

questions.prompt: The simplified numerical value of √[4]{(81)<sup>-2</sup>} is:
questions.answer: (b) 1/9
questions.examinerTip: Apply law of exponents (a^m)^n = a^(mn).

questions.prompt: If x<sup>51</sup> + 51 is divided by (x + 1), then the remainder is:
questions.answer: (c) 50
questions.markingScheme: • By Remainder Theorem, R = p(-1) = (-1)<sup>51</sup> + 51 = -1 + 51 = 50 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: (-1) raised to an odd power is always -1.

questions.prompt: A point P has ordinate 4 and lies on the y-axis. If point P is reflected across the x-axis to form P', the coordinates of P' are:
questions.answer: (c) (0, -4)
questions.markingScheme: • On y-axis, x = 0, so P is (0, 4). Reflection across x-axis negates y-coordinate: (0, -4) [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Reflection across x-axis transforms (x, y) → (x, -y).

questions.prompt: If x + 1/x = 5, then the value of x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> is:
questions.answer: (c) 23
questions.markingScheme: • (x + 1/x)<sup>2</sup> = x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> + 2 ⇒ 25 = x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> + 2 ⇒ x<sup>2</sup> + 1/x<sup>2</sup> = 23 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Always subtract 2 × x × (1/x) = 2 when squaring a reciprocal sum.

questions.prompt: The perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 60 m. Its area is:
questions.answer: (a) 100√3 m2
questions.markingScheme: • Side a = 60/3 = 20 m. Area = (√3/4) × a<sup>2</sup> = (√3/4) × 400 = 100√3 m<sup>2</sup> [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Area of equilateral triangle formula is (√3 / 4) × a^2.

questions.prompt: The distance between the points A(0, 6) and B(0, -2) on the Cartesian plane is:
questions.answer: (c) 8 units
questions.markingScheme: • Points share x = 0 (vertical line). Distance = |y2 - y1| = |6 - (-2)| = 8 units [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: For points on the same vertical axis, distance is the absolute difference of ordinates.

questions.prompt: Which of the following expressions is exactly equal to √5 - √3?
questions.answer: (a) 2 / (√5 + √3)
questions.markingScheme: • Rationalizing: 2 / (√5 + √3) = 2(√5 - √3) / (5 - 3) = 2(√5 - √3) / 2 = √5 - √3 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Conjugate multiplication simplifies (a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2.

questions.prompt: The graph of the linear equation 2x + 3y = 6 intersects the x-axis at the point:
questions.answer: (b) (3, 0)
questions.markingScheme: • Put y = 0 ⇒ 2x + 3(0) = 6 ⇒ 2x = 6 ⇒ x = 3. Point is (3, 0) [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Every point on the x-axis has ordinate y = 0.

questions.prompt: If the numerical values of the perimeter and the area of a circle are equal, then the radius of the circle is:
questions.answer: (b) 2 units
questions.markingScheme: • 2πr = πr<sup>2</sup> ⇒ 2r = r<sup>2</sup> (since r ≠ 0) ⇒ r = 2 units [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Divide both sides by πr since radius cannot be zero.

questions.prompt: The degree of the zero polynomial p(x) = 0 is:
questions.answer: (d) Not defined
questions.markingScheme: • The zero polynomial 0 = 0 × x<sup>n</sup> has no unique exponent, hence its degree is undefined [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: A non-zero constant polynomial like p(x) = 5 has degree 0, but the zero polynomial has undefined degree.

questions.prompt: If M(2, 3) is the midpoint of the line segment joining A(4, 5) and B(x, y), then the coordinates of B are:
questions.answer: (a) (0, 1)
questions.markingScheme: • x_M = (x_A + x_B)/2 ⇒ 2 = (4 + x)/2 ⇒ x = 0; y_M = (y_A + y_B)/2 ⇒ 3 = (5 + y)/2 ⇒ y = 1 ⇒ (0, 1) [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Reverse midpoint formula: x_B = 2x_M - x_A and y_B = 2y_M - y_A.

questions.prompt: Which of the following numbers is an irrational number lying strictly between 1/7 (0.142857...) and 2/7 (0.285714...)?
questions.markingScheme: • 0.150150015... is non-terminating and non-repeating (irrational) and 0.1428 < 0.1501 < 0.2857 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Non-terminating, non-repeating decimal patterns guarantee irrationality.

questions.prompt: If a + b + c = 0, then the value of (a<sup>2</sup> / bc) + (b<sup>2</sup> / ca) + (c<sup>2</sup> / ab) is:
questions.answer: (c) 3
questions.markingScheme: • Common denominator abc gives (a<sup>3</sup> + b<sup>3</sup> + c<sup>3</sup>)/abc. When a+b+c=0, a<sup>3</sup>+b<sup>3</sup>+c<sup>3</sup> = 3abc. Hence 3abc/abc = 3 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Standard algebraic identity application: a+b+c=0 ⇒ a^3+b^3+c^3 = 3abc.

questions.prompt: The sides of a triangle are in the ratio 12 : 17 : 25 and its perimeter is 540 cm. The length of the shortest side is:
questions.answer: (a) 120 cm
questions.markingScheme: • 12x + 17x + 25x = 54x = 540 ⇒ x = 10 cm. Shortest side = 12(10) = 120 cm [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Always sum ratio parts to find common multiplier x.

questions.prompt: If the coordinates of two points are P(-2, 3) and Q(-3, 5), then (abscissa of P) - (abscissa of Q) is:
questions.answer: (b) 1
questions.markingScheme: • Abscissa of P = -2. Abscissa of Q = -3. Difference = -2 - (-3) = -2 + 3 = 1 [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Abscissa refers strictly to the x-coordinate.

questions.prompt: A linear equation in two variables ax + by + c = 0 (where a ≠ 0, b ≠ 0) has:
questions.answer: (c) Infinitely many solutions
questions.markingScheme: • Every linear equation in two variables represents a straight line with infinitely many coordinate points lying on it [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: For every chosen value of x, there exists a unique corresponding y on the line.

questions.prompt: In a circle of radius 7 cm, the length of an arc that subtends an angle of 60° at the center is (take π = 22/7):
questions.answer: (a) 22/3 cm
questions.markingScheme: • Arc length L = (θ/360°) × 2πr = (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 7 = (1/6) × 44 = 22/3 cm [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Arc length is proportional to the fraction of the full 360-degree rotation.

questions.prompt:
Assertion (A): 0.27̅ (with bar on 7) is a rational number.
Reason (R): Every decimal number having a non-terminating repeating expansion can be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.answer: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.markingScheme: • 0.2777... = (27-2)/90 = 25/90 = 5/18 (rational). Non-terminating repeating decimals are rational by definition in (R) [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Bar notation denotes recurring decimals, which are rational numbers.

questions.prompt:
Assertion (A): The polynomial p(x) = x2 - 4x + 4 has exactly one distinct zero.
Reason (R): Every quadratic polynomial must have two distinct real zeroes.
options: (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.answer: (c) (A) is true but (R) is false.
questions.markingScheme: • p(x) = (x - 2)<sup>2</sup> has only one unique real zero (x = 2). A quadratic can have 2, 1, or 0 real zeroes, so (R) is false [1 mark]
questions.examinerTip: Equal roots mean only one distinct zero.

questions.prompt:
Find the values of rational numbers a and b if:
(√3 - 1) / (√3 + 1) = a + b√3.
questions.answer:
Multiply numerator and denominator by conjugate (√3 - 1):
= (√3 - 1)2 / [(√3 + 1)(√3 - 1)]
= (3 - 2√3 + 1) / (3 - 1)
= (4 - 2√3) / 2 = 2 - √3.

Equating with a + b√3:
a = 2 and b = -1.
questions.markingScheme:
• Multiplying by conjugate and expanding numerator: 1 mark
• Dividing by 2 to get 2 - √3: 0.5 mark
• Stating a = 2, b = -1: 0.5 mark
questions.examinerTip: Do not forget that the coefficient of √3 is negative, so b = -1, not 1.

questions.prompt:
Points A(2, 3), B(-2, 3), C(-2, -3), and D(2, -3) are plotted on a Cartesian plane. Join them in order to form quadrilateral ABCD.
(i) Name the type of quadrilateral formed.
(ii) Find its perimeter and area.
questions.answer:
(i) Length AB = |2 - (-2)| = 4 units (horizontal).
Length BC = |3 - (-3)| = 6 units (vertical).
Length CD = |2 - (-2)| = 4 units.
Length DA = |3 - (-3)| = 6 units.
Adjacent sides are perpendicular (parallel to axes). Hence ABCD is a Rectangle.

(ii) Perimeter = 2(length + breadth) = 2(6 + 4) = 20 units.
Area = length × breadth = 6 × 4 = 24 square units.
questions.markingScheme:
• Identifying Rectangle with side lengths 4 and 6: 1 mark
• Perimeter = 20 units: 0.5 mark
• Area = 24 sq units: 0.5 mark
questions.examinerTip: Coordinates aligned with axes have side lengths equal to absolute coordinate differences.

questions.prompt:
Evaluate without direct cubing using algebraic identities:
(28)3 + (-15)3 + (-13)3.
questions.answer:
Let a = 28, b = -15, c = -13.
Compute sum: a + b + c = 28 + (-15) + (-13) = 28 - 28 = 0.

Since a + b + c = 0, we have the identity:
a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Therefore:
(28)3 + (-15)3 + (-13)3 = 3(28)(-15)(-13)
= 84 × 195 = 16,380.
questions.markingScheme:
• Verifying a + b + c = 0: 0.5 mark
• Stating identity a3+b3+c3 = 3abc: 0.5 mark
• Correct evaluation 3 × 28 × (-15) × (-13) = 16,380: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Product of two negative terms is positive: (-15) × (-13) = +195.

questions.prompt: Find the value of k if the linear equation 2x - 3y = k passes through the point of intersection of the vertical line x = 4 and the horizontal line y = -1.
questions.answer:
The intersection point of x = 4 and y = -1 is (4, -1).

Substitute x = 4 and y = -1 into 2x - 3y = k:
2(4) - 3(-1) = k
8 + 3 = k
k = 11.
questions.markingScheme:
• Stating point of intersection (4, -1): 1 mark
• Substituting into equation and finding k = 11: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Vertical and horizontal lines intersect at (constant x, constant y).

questions.prompt: An isosceles right-angled triangle has an area of 8 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the length of its hypotenuse.
questions.answer:
Let the two equal legs be of length a cm.
Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × a × a = a2 / 2.
Given a2 / 2 = 8 ⇒ a2 = 16 ⇒ a = 4 cm.

By Baudh&amacron;yana-Pythagoras theorem:
Hypotenuse h = √(a2 + a2) = √(16 + 16) = √32 = 4√2 cm (or approx 5.66 cm).
questions.markingScheme:
• Setting up (1/2)a2 = 8 to find a = 4 cm: 1 mark
• Calculating hypotenuse h = √(42 + 42) = 4√2 cm: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: In an isosceles right triangle, hypotenuse is always equal to side × √2.

questions.prompt: Represent √9.3 geometrically on the number line and write the steps of construction.
questions.answer:
Steps of Construction:
1. Draw a line segment AB = 9.3 units on a straight line.
2. Extend AB by 1 unit to point C such that BC = 1 unit. Total AC = 10.3 units.
3. Find the midpoint O of AC by drawing perpendicular bisector of AC (radius OA = OC = 10.3/2 = 5.15 units).
4. With O as center and radius OA, draw a semicircle passing through A and C.
5. Draw a line perpendicular to AC at point B, cutting the semicircle at point D.
6. By Pythagoras theorem, length BD = √9.3 units.
7. With B as origin (0) and radius BD, draw an arc intersecting the number line at point E. Point E represents √9.3.
questions.markingScheme:
• Steps 1-3 (Drawing AB=9.3, BC=1, finding midpoint O): 1 mark
• Steps 4-5 (Semicircle and perpendicular BD): 1 mark
• Mathematical justification OD2 - OB2 = BD2 ⇒ BD = √9.3: 1 mark

questions.prompt: If (x - 1) and (x + 2) are factors of the polynomial p(x) = x<sup>3</sup> + ax<sup>2</sup> + bx - 6, find the values of a and b. Hence, find the third linear factor of p(x).
questions.answer:
1. Since (x - 1) is a factor, p(1) = 0:
13 + a(1)2 + b(1) - 6 = 0 ⇒ 1 + a + b - 6 = 0 ⇒ a + b = 5 --- (Eq 1)

2. Since (x + 2) is a factor, p(-2) = 0:
(-2)3 + a(-2)2 + b(-2) - 6 = 0 ⇒ -8 + 4a - 2b - 6 = 0 ⇒ 4a - 2b = 14 ⇒ 2a - b = 7 --- (Eq 2)

3. Add Eq 1 and Eq 2:
(a + b) + (2a - b) = 5 + 7 ⇒ 3a = 12 ⇒ a = 4.
From Eq 1: 4 + b = 5 ⇒ b = 1.

4. The polynomial is p(x) = x3 + 4x2 + x - 6.
Known product of factors = (x - 1)(x + 2) = x2 + x - 2.
Dividing p(x) by (x2 + x - 2):
(x3 + 4x2 + x - 6) = (x2 + x - 2)(x + 3).
Therefore, the third factor is (x + 3).
questions.markingScheme:
• Forming Eq 1 (a + b = 5): 1 mark
• Forming Eq 2 (2a - b = 7) and solving for a = 4, b = 1: 1 mark
• Finding third factor (x + 3): 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Constant term check: (-1) × (+2) × (+3) = -6, which matches the constant term.

questions.prompt: If point P(x, y) is equidistant from the points A(5, 1) and B(-1, 5), prove that 3x = 2y.
questions.answer:
Given PA = PB ⇒ PA2 = PB2.

Using the Baudh&amacron;yana-Pythagoras distance formula:
PA2 = (x - 5)2 + (y - 1)2 = x2 - 10x + 25 + y2 - 2y + 1 = x2 + y2 - 10x - 2y + 26.

PB2 = (x - (-1))2 + (y - 5)2 = (x + 1)2 + (y - 5)2 = x2 + 2x + 1 + y2 - 10y + 25 = x2 + y2 + 2x - 10y + 26.

Equating PA2 = PB2:
x2 + y2 - 10x - 2y + 26 = x2 + y2 + 2x - 10y + 26
-10x - 2y = 2x - 10y
-10x - 2x = -10y + 2y
-12x = -8y
Divide both sides by -4:
3x = 2y. (Hence Proved).
questions.markingScheme:
• Expanding PA2 and PB2: 1.5 marks
• Cancelling common terms and simplifying: 1 mark
• Reaching 3x = 2y: 0.5 mark
questions.examinerTip: Always square distances first (PA^2 = PB^2) to eliminate the square root radical.

questions.prompt:
For the linear equation 3x + 2y = 12:
(i) Find the points where its graph cuts the x-axis and the y-axis.
(ii) Calculate the area of the triangle formed by this straight line with the coordinate axes.
questions.answer:
(i) To find the x-intercept: put y = 0:
3x + 2(0) = 12 ⇒ 3x = 12 ⇒ x = 4. Point A is (4, 0).
To find the y-intercept: put x = 0:
3(0) + 2y = 12 ⇒ 2y = 12 ⇒ y = 6. Point B is (0, 6).

(ii) The coordinate axes meet at origin O(0, 0) at a right angle (90°).
ΔOAB is a right-angled triangle with base OA = 4 units and height OB = 6 units.
Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 4 × 6 = 12 square units.
questions.markingScheme:
• Finding (4, 0) and (0, 6): 1.5 marks
• Right-triangle area formula (1/2 × OA × OB): 0.5 mark
• Area = 12 sq units: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Triangle formed with axes always has area = (1/2) × |x-intercept| × |y-intercept|.

questions.prompt:
A triangular park has sides 120 m, 80 m, and 50 m. A gardener has to put a fence all around it leaving a space 3 m wide for a gate on one side.
(i) Find the total length and cost of fencing at the rate of ₹20 per meter. (1.5m)
(ii) Find the area of the park using Heron's formula. (1.5m)
questions.answer:
(i) Perimeter = 120 + 80 + 50 = 250 m.
Length of fence required = Perimeter - Gate width = 250 - 3 = 247 m.
Cost of fencing = 247 × ₹20 = ₹4,940.

(ii) Semi-perimeter s = 250 / 2 = 125 m.
s - a = 125 - 120 = 5 m
s - b = 125 - 80 = 45 m
s - c = 125 - 50 = 75 m.
Area = √[125 × 5 × 45 × 75]
= √[(25 × 5) × 5 × (9 × 5) × (25 × 3)]
= √[252 × 52 × 9 × 15]
= 25 × 5 × 3 × √15 = 375√15 m2 (approx 1452.37 m2).
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Net fencing length 247 m and cost ₹4,940: 1.5 marks
• (ii) s = 125 m and Heron's formula factoring Area = 375√15 m2: 1.5 marks
questions.examinerTip: Remember to subtract the 3m gate before calculating the fencing cost.

questions.prompt: Factorize completely using algebraic identities: x6 - 64.
questions.answer:
1. Express as difference of squares first (preferable over cubes):
x6 - 64 = (x3)2 - (8)2
= (x3 - 8)(x3 + 8)

2. Apply difference of cubes to (x3 - 8):
x3 - 23 = (x - 2)(x2 + 2x + 4)

3. Apply sum of cubes to (x3 + 8):
x3 + 23 = (x + 2)(x2 - 2x + 4)

4. Combining all factors:
(x - 2)(x + 2)(x2 + 2x + 4)(x2 - 2x + 4).
questions.markingScheme:
• Difference of squares (x3 - 8)(x3 + 8): 1 mark
• Factoring (x3 - 8): 1 mark
• Factoring (x3 + 8) and final four-factor product: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Factoring difference of squares first produces cleaner, irreducible quadratic factors.

questions.prompt:
If x = 3 + 2√2, evaluate the following step-by-step:
(i) 1/x (1m)
(ii) x + 1/x (1m)
(iii) x2 + 1/x2 (1m)
(iv) x3 + 1/x3 (1m)
(v) √x + 1/√x (1m)
questions.answer:
(i) 1/x = 1 / (3 + 2√2) = (3 - 2√2) / [32 - (2√2)2] = (3 - 2√2) / (9 - 8) = 3 - 2√2.

(ii) x + 1/x = (3 + 2√2) + (3 - 2√2) = 6.

(iii) x2 + 1/x2 = (x + 1/x)2 - 2 = 62 - 2 = 36 - 2 = 34.

(iv) x3 + 1/x3 = (x + 1/x)3 - 3(x + 1/x) = 63 - 3(6) = 216 - 18 = 198.

(v) Let u = √x + 1/√x.
u2 = (√x + 1/√x)2 = x + 1/x + 2 = 6 + 2 = 8.
Since x > 0, √x + 1/√x > 0 ⇒ u = √8 = 2√2.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) 1/x = 3 - 2√2: 1 mark
• (ii) x + 1/x = 6: 1 mark
• (iii) x2 + 1/x2 = 34: 1 mark
• (iv) x3 + 1/x3 = 198: 1 mark
• (v) √x + 1/√x = 2√2: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Notice how all sub-parts cascade naturally once x + 1/x = 6 is computed.

questions.prompt: A field is in the shape of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 25 m and 10 m, and non-parallel sides are 14 m and 13 m. Find the area of the field by decomposing it into a parallelogram and a triangle.
questions.answer:
1. Let trapezium be ABCD with AB = 25 m, CD = 10 m (parallel), AD = 13 m, BC = 14 m.
2. Draw CE parallel to DA meeting AB at E.
Then AECD is a parallelogram ⇒ AE = CD = 10 m and CE = AD = 13 m.
3. Length EB = AB - AE = 25 - 10 = 15 m.
Now ΔCEB has sides: CE = 13 m, BC = 14 m, EB = 15 m.

4. Compute area of ΔCEB by Heron's formula:
Semi-perimeter s = (13 + 14 + 15)/2 = 42/2 = 21 m.
s - 13 = 8, s - 14 = 7, s - 15 = 6.
Area(ΔCEB) = √[21 × 8 × 7 × 6] = √[(7 × 3) × 8 × 7 × (2 × 3)] = √[72 × 32 × 16] = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 m2.

5. Let h be height of ΔCEB (which is also height of trapezium):
Area(ΔCEB) = (1/2) × base × h ⇒ 84 = (1/2) × 15 × h ⇒ h = 168/15 = 11.2 m.

6. Area of Trapezium = (1/2) × (sum of parallel sides) × h
= (1/2) × (25 + 10) × 11.2 = (1/2) × 35 × 11.2 = 35 × 5.6 = 196 m2.
questions.markingScheme:
• Geometric decomposition into parallelogram and triangle with side 15 m: 1.5 marks
• Heron's area of triangle CEB = 84 m2: 1.5 marks
• Height h = 11.2 m: 1 mark
• Total trapezium area = 196 m2: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Classic NCERT HOTS problem. Area can also be found as Area(Parallelogram) + Area(Triangle) = (10 × 11.2) + 84 = 112 + 84 = 196 m^2.

questions.prompt: If x + y + z = 1, xy + yz + zx = -1, and xyz = -1, find the value of x<sup>3</sup> + y<sup>3</sup> + z<sup>3</sup>.
questions.answer:
1. Recall the standard identity:
x3 + y3 + z3 - 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x2 + y2 + z2 - xy - yz - zx) --- (1)

2. We need x2 + y2 + z2:
(x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)
12 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(-1)
1 = x2 + y2 + z2 - 2
x2 + y2 + z2 = 3.

3. Compute (x2 + y2 + z2 - (xy + yz + zx)):
= 3 - (-1) = 3 + 1 = 4.

4. Substitute into identity (1):
x3 + y3 + z3 - 3(-1) = (1) × (4)
x3 + y3 + z3 + 3 = 4
x3 + y3 + z3 = 4 - 3
x3 + y3 + z3 = 1.
questions.markingScheme:
• Stating identity: 1 mark
• Finding x2 + y2 + z2 = 3: 2 marks
• Substituting all terms into identity: 1 mark
• Final answer 1: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Carefully track negative signs: - 3xyz becomes - 3(-1) = +3.

questions.prompt:
The coordinates of the midpoints of the sides of ΔABC are D(3, 4), E(4, 6), and F(2, 5), where D, E, F are the midpoints of BC, CA, and AB respectively.
(i) Reconstruct the coordinates of vertices A, B, and C. (3m)
(ii) Find the length of the side BC using the Baudh&amacron;yana-Pythagoras distance formula. (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) By the NCERT Ganita Manjari Midpoint Reconstruction Theorem:
For vertex A: opposite midpoint is D(3, 4), adjacent midpoints are E(4, 6) and F(2, 5):
x_A = x_E + x_F - x_D = 4 + 2 - 3 = 3.
y_A = y_E + y_F - y_D = 6 + 5 - 4 = 7.
So, A(3, 7).

For vertex B: opposite midpoint is E(4, 6), adjacent are D(3, 4) and F(2, 5):
x_B = x_D + x_F - x_E = 3 + 2 - 4 = 1.
y_B = y_D + y_F - y_E = 4 + 5 - 6 = 3.
So, B(1, 3).

For vertex C: opposite midpoint is F(2, 5), adjacent are D(3, 4) and E(4, 6):
x_C = x_D + x_E - x_F = 3 + 4 - 2 = 5.
y_C = y_D + y_E - y_F = 4 + 6 - 5 = 5.
So, C(5, 5).

(ii) Side BC connects B(1, 3) and C(5, 5):
d(BC) = √[(5 - 1)2 + (5 - 3)2]
= √[42 + 22] = √[16 + 4] = √20 = 2√5 units (approx 4.47 units).
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Formula x_A = x_E + x_F - x_D and finding A(3, 7): 1 mark
• Finding B(1, 3) and C(5, 5): 2 marks
• (ii) Applying distance formula for BC: 1 mark
• BC = √20 = 2√5 units: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Direct application of NCERT Ganita Manjari Chapter 1 midpoint reconstruction theorem.

questions.prompt:
An architect is planning an exhibition pavilion using physical Algebra Tiles to model modular floor spaces. The layout requires 1 large square zone of side x meters (area x2), 7 rectangular passage strips of dimensions x × 1 meters, and 10 small unit storage squares of side 1 meter.

Questions:
(i) Write the polynomial A(x) representing the total floor area. (1m)
(ii) Factorize A(x) into two linear binomial dimensions representing length and breadth. (1m)
(iii) If x = 8 meters, calculate the numerical length, breadth, and total floor area. If carpet installation costs ₹250 per m2, find the total cost. (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) Total Area polynomial A(x) = 1(x2) + 7(x) + 10(1) = x2 + 7x + 10.

(ii) Splitting the middle term (factors of 10 that sum to 7 are 5 and 2):
x2 + 5x + 2x + 10 = x(x + 5) + 2(x + 5) = (x + 5)(x + 2).
So the dimensions are Length = (x + 5) m and Breadth = (x + 2) m.

(iii) For x = 8 m:
Length = 8 + 5 = 13 m.
Breadth = 8 + 2 = 10 m.
Total Area = 13 × 10 = 130 m2.
Total Flooring Cost = 130 × ₹250 = ₹32,500.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) Polynomial x2 + 7x + 10: 1 mark
• (ii) Factoring (x + 5)(x + 2): 1 mark
• (iii) Dimensions 13m × 10m, area 130 m2, and cost ₹32,500: 2 marks
questions.examinerTip: Algebra tiles geometrically justify the splitting-of-the-middle-term technique.

questions.prompt:
A modern drone delivery network maps its operations over a city grid measured in kilometers. The central control dispatch tower is located at the origin O(0, 0). Two primary hospital receiving hubs are situated at P(6, 8) and Q(-6, 8).

Questions:
(i) Calculate the direct flight distance from dispatch O(0, 0) to hub P(6, 8) using the Baudh&amacron;yana-Pythagoras distance formula. (1m)
(ii) Determine the coordinates of waypoint M, which is the exact midpoint between hospital hubs P and Q. (1m)
(iii) A solar recharge relay R is located at (0, 16). Verify whether dispatch tower O(0, 0), waypoint M, and relay R are collinear. What is the total flight path distance from O to P and then P to R? (2m)
questions.answer:
(i) Distance OP = √[(6 - 0)2 + (8 - 0)2] = √[36 + 64] = √100 = 10 km.

(ii) Midpoint M = ((6 + (-6))/2, (8 + 8)/2) = (0/2, 16/2) = (0, 8).

(iii) All three points O(0, 0), M(0, 8), and R(0, 16) have x-coordinate equal to 0. Since their abscissa is constant 0, they all lie on the y-axis, hence they are Collinear.
Distance PR = √[(0 - 6)2 + (16 - 8)2] = √[(-6)2 + 82] = √[36 + 64] = √100 = 10 km.
Total flight distance O → P → R = OP + PR = 10 km + 10 km = 20 km.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) OP = 10 km: 1 mark
• (ii) M(0, 8): 1 mark
• (iii) Collinearity justification (x = 0 / y-axis): 1 mark; Total distance 20 km: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Points lying on the same coordinate axis or line x = c are immediately collinear.

questions.prompt:
An agricultural research station manages a triangular test plantation plot whose boundary lengths are a = 35 m, b = 53 m, and c = 66 m.

Questions:
(i) Calculate the semi-perimeter s of the plantation plot. (1m)
(ii) Calculate the total area of the triangular plot using Heron's formula. (2m)
(iii) A central rotary sprinkler irrigates a circular area of radius r = 7 m inside this plot. Calculate the remaining unirrigated area of the plantation (take π = 22/7). (1m)
questions.answer:
(i) Semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2 = (35 + 53 + 66)/2 = 154/2 = 77 m.

(ii) Applying Heron's formula:
s - a = 77 - 35 = 42 m
s - b = 77 - 53 = 24 m
s - c = 77 - 66 = 11 m.
Area = √[s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)] = √[77 × 42 × 24 × 11]
= √[(7 × 11) × (7 × 6) × (6 × 4) × 11]
= √[72 × 112 × 62 × 22]
= 7 × 11 × 6 × 2 = 77 × 12 = 924 m2.

(iii) Circular irrigated area = πr2 = (22/7) × 7 × 7 = 154 m2.
Remaining unirrigated area = Total Area - Irrigated Area = 924 - 154 = 770 m2.
questions.markingScheme:
• (i) s = 77 m: 1 mark
• (ii) Heron's formula factoring and Area = 924 m2: 2 marks
• (iii) Circle area 154 m2 and remaining area 770 m2: 1 mark
questions.examinerTip: Factor 77 = 7 × 11 and 42 = 7 × 6 to easily pair up perfect squares under the radical.
